- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if followed by a spike.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and model shows strong upward trend, cap forecast at 1–2% below recent high to avoid overcorrection.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots; apply a 3–5 day lag correction by reducing forecast by 2–5% per day post-spike.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish, model frequently fails to adjust downward; apply a 1–3 day mean reversion buffer to forecast.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, flag for downward adjustment unless sentiment is strong bullish.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >5% from model in first 5 days, adjust forecast downward by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.33–0.67 oscillation, model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast with 3-day moving average unless sentiment is trending.
